analysis.title: Americas Technology: Semiconductors. At the center of tensions around the AI datacenter build: Searching for value following the sector-wide pullback
key_insights: GS says two tensions are driving semis. One is how the gap between hyperscaler and AI-lab capex and their free cash flow gets closed. The other is whether enough land, power and shell capacity is coming online to match Street semi estimates.

After the Nov. 3 US elections, uncertainty about the pace of datacenter builds in states such as Texas pushed SOX down 13% in the past week and 31% since Oct. 1. GS calls the sector clearly oversold and sees compelling risk/reward in select names, though it expects few catalysts before year end.

GS estimates AI infrastructure capex of about $1.3 trillion in 2027 (up 60% YoY) and $2.0 trillion in 2028 (up 42% YoY). This covers hyperscalers, AI labs, sovereign AI and enterprise customers. It implies about 20 GW, 35 GW and 57 GW of AI datacenter deployments in 2026, 2027 and 2028.

Per-GW revenue assumptions: Broadcom $20-30 billion per GW (guiding to 10 GW in FY27 and 20 GW in FY28), Nvidia about $25 billion per GW for Blackwell rising to about $40 billion for Rubin (about $45 billion with Feynman), AMD $15-20 billion per GW.

GS sees about 35 GW of 2027 datacenter builds as relatively low risk. For 2028 it treats another 35 GW as a low-risk floor, with 55-60 GW if construction projects proceed. Under-construction US additions of 22/24/5 GW-IT for 2027/28/29 compare with GS forecasts of 20/24/23 GW-IT.

Texas is 20% of 2027E and 27% of 2028E net additions among under-construction capacity, and 26% of 2026-30 cumulative net additions. GS notes the Governor-elect has called for an immediate moratorium on data centers. It says moratoria are not bans or cancellations, the main risks are delays to ready-for-service and higher costs, and any moratorium would likely apply to new rather than under-construction sites.

The SOX drawdown relative to the S&P 500 is now approaching 30 points, a ten-year record. Only twice before did it exceed 20 points, and those drawdowns were typically followed by outperformance. GS calls the current level a good index-level entry point but warns resolution may take time given heavy de-grossing around year end.

AI compute: GS favors NVDA and AVGO, which it says imply no growth from 2027. Even with no growth in 2028 (seen as unlikely), NVDA and AVGO trade at 12X and 13X that baseline. AMD is seen as very attractive on growth but at a less compelling valuation.
Scenarios for 2028 deployments: Bear Case #2 at 35 GW (the floor), Bear Case #1 at 45 GW, base case 57 GW, bull case 65 GW. Company estimates are flexed proportionally to GW.

Semi cap equipment: GS treats 2027 WFE as a baseline and prefers AMAT and LRCX at 15X and 16X 2027E EPS. It says capacity coming online through 2028 is catching up to past demand. Tokyo Electron also screens attractive. Scenarios assume 2028 WFE growth of about 30%, about 15%, or flat.

Memory: global memory stocks have historically bottomed around tangible book value. Samsung and SK Hynix are approaching it and are already below total book. Micron (Neutral) is at about 5.4x tangible book and could fall well below it over coming quarters on GS's projected FCF. GS sees risk/reward improving on the high probability of strong FCF.

Price targets: NVDA $300, AVGO $540, AMD $675, AMAT $670, LRCX $380, KLAC $195 (Neutral), MU $1,250 (Neutral), TER $440, MediaTek NT$7,100, Samsung W500,000, SK Hynix W3,500,000, Tokyo Electron ¥19,000. Marvell is Not Rated because GS is a financial advisor on an announced strategic matter.

sector_views.rationale: NVDA and AVGO screen attractive across downside GW scenarios, with 2027 deployments of about 35 GW seen as low risk.
2027 WFE is treated as a baseline. AMAT and LRCX trade at 15X and 16X 2027E EPS and capacity additions through 2028 are seen as catching up to past demand.
Stocks are approaching oversold levels near tangible book. GS sees improving risk/reward on strong expected FCF but keeps Micron at Neutral.

earnings_insights: GS sees a high probability of strong free cash flow at Micron (Neutral) in coming quarters. Its projected FCF could push tangible book value per share well above the current price over upcoming quarters.
GS price targets rest on normalized EPS estimates: NVDA $10.00, AVGO $18.00, AMD $22.50, AMAT $21.00, LRCX $10.75, KLAC $6.50, MU $70.00, TER $12.50. These are GS forecasts and not reported figures.
In the semi cap scenario analysis, 2028 EPS estimates assume about 30% WFE growth in 2028 for Scenario 1 and about 15% for Scenario 2. Scenario 3 uses 2027 EPS with flat 2028 WFE.

trade_ideas.rationale: Both trade at 12X and 13X a no-growth 2028 baseline and imply no growth from 2027.
trade_ideas.risk: Slowdown in AI infrastructure spending, competitive share erosion, delays in datacenter builds.

trade_ideas.rationale: Trading at 15X and 16X 2027E EPS, compelling even with no capex growth beyond 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Memory entry as stocks approach tangible book value, with Micron cited as improving risk/reward on FCF

risk_factors: Delays to ready-for-service and higher costs for datacenter operators if a Texas moratorium is implemented.
Announced but not under-construction capacity is the key driver of 2028 upside and 2029-30 growth, and carries higher risk.
Few catalysts before year end and heavy de-grossing may keep semis pressured near term.
Slowdown in AI infrastructure spending and the unresolved funding gap between capex and free cash flow at hyperscalers and AI labs.
Export restrictions and Chinese competition, including CXMT in DRAM.

GS flags significant de-grossing in the broader market, particularly around year end, which may delay a recovery in semis.
SOX is down 13% in the past week and 31% since Oct. 1, which GS calls clearly oversold.
Memory price to tangible book: SK Hynix about 3.1x, Samsung about 1.8x, Micron about 5.4x. Samsung and SK Hynix are below total book.
geopolitical: US elections on Nov. 3 raised uncertainty about datacenter build pace in states such as Texas.
Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa called for an immediate moratorium on data centers.
Incremental US export restrictions on China and local China-based supplier share gains are cited as risks for AMAT, KLAC and Tokyo Electron.
CXMT gaining DRAM market share in China is cited as a risk to memory pricing.

tension_points.bull_case: GS sees about 35 GW of 2027 deployments as already largely in progress and low risk, and a 35 GW 2028 floor. It says NVDA and AVGO trade at 12X and 13X even with no growth in 2028, and that AMAT and LRCX at 15X and 16X 2027E EPS are compelling with no capex increase beyond 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Uncertainty over land, power and shell supply, plus a Texas moratorium call, could delay datacenter builds. Texas is 20% of 2027E and 27% of 2028E under-construction net additions. The funding gap between hyperscaler and AI-lab capex and free cash flow is also unresolved, and 2028 upside depends on higher-risk announced capacity.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Deployments falling below the 35 GW 2028 floor that GS treats as low risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Moratoria are not bans or cancellations and would likely apply to new data centers rather than those under construction, so under-construction capacity is lower risk.
tension_points.bear_case: The key risks to data center operators are delays to ready-for-service and higher costs, and Texas is 26% of 2026-30 cumulative net additions.
